raw.assessment: The incumbent honored all designs and uses a reference-table check to catch errors, but seven covers required resewing and median time exceeded the target. Rework concentrated in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium and 0/18 small), consistent with a size-dependent fitting problem; allowance, operator, direction and cloth effects remain unresolved. The concrete limitation is that both observed customer placement failures involved rounded corners absent from reference tables: passing the existing check does not establish customer fit. Small-cover times establish feasibility only for that subgroup. Estimated waste by weight does not establish compliance with the area limit.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create systematic fit error as table size increases, making early size-specific calibration useful.
openings.delta: Sew and inspect initial examples before cutting the remaining stock; change allowances only if measured errors support doing so.
openings.prediction: Under matched cloth direction and operator, finished dimensional error increases with size; a calibrated allowance reduces that error and resewing on a subsequent large cover.
openings.probe: Record order, cut and finished dimensions and stage times on initial covers across sizes. Measure offcut length and width through the stipulated wash test. Trial any correction on the next comparable ordered cover; calculate layout waste by area before cutting. Include calibration labor when assessing batch time.
assumptions: A corrected layout fits purchased stock within 8% area waste.
Calibration and validation fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget.

openings.claim: Do rounded corners cause first-placement failures independently of inaccurate nominal length and width?
openings.delta: Test the specific geometry missing from the reference-table check before changing corner-pocket construction.
openings.prediction: If corner geometry matters independently, nominally matching rounded tables still fail when actual length and width match; if dimension error explains failures, placement follows dimensional mismatch instead.
openings.probe: Ask the six willing customers for actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Observe first placement and compare tables with similar measured dimensions but different corners. Treat absent matched comparisons as inconclusive. Validate any resulting pocket revision for the ordered design, tool-free removal and five-cycle wash survival before adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include informative geometry comparisons.
Measurements and installation observations are sufficiently consistent.

raw.assessment: The size concentration of seam rework and the customer corner mismatch suggest two distinguishable fitting problems. Neither cause is established. Missing stage timings and width shrinkage prevent a justified claim that either opening will achieve 38 of 40 first placements and a median of 32 minutes.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: sew and check the first ordered cover in each size before releasing that size's remaining cutting, using measured deviations to assess the common allowance.
openings.delta: Replace whole-batch cutting with a size-specific feedback point; the first covers remain saleable batch units.
openings.prediction: If the common allowance drives rework, comparable cut-to-sewn dimensional errors should recur by size, and correcting the demonstrated error should reduce later same-size seam reopening. Inconsistent errors would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Record actual cut dimensions, sewn dimensions, operator, cutting direction, design and stage times for the first unit of each size and subsequent units. Release any revised cutting card only after checking fit, five-cycle wash survival and a stock layout with no more than 8% waste by area; count trial and coordination labor in batch working time.
assumptions: A usable correction can fit the purchased stock and delivery window.
The first unit provides useful information despite operator and cloth variation.

openings.claim: Customer table dimensions and corner profiles may explain installation failures that the reference-table check misses.
openings.delta: Validate the order-to-actual-table match before treating reference-table fit as sufficient.
openings.prediction: Among covers passing the reference check, customer placement difficulty should concentrate where measured dimensions or corner profiles differ from the reference, rather than solely by cover size.
openings.probe: Use the six willing customers to obtain actual tabletop dimensions and corner outlines, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Pair those measurements with reference fit and observed first placement. Record dimension mismatch separately from corner mismatch to distinguish their associations.
assumptions: Customers can supply sufficiently accurate measurements within three weeks.
Measurement and observation effort fits the existing budget and is included in working time.

openings.claim: Common allowance may cause size-dependent rework; check the first saleable ordered cover per size before releasing remaining cutting.
openings.discriminator: Recurring size-linked dimensional errors under comparable operator, design and direction support allowance correction; inconsistent errors weaken it. Subsequent comparable covers test reduced resewing.
openings.fit: Uncertain: corrected layouts, calibration and validation must satisfy stock, waste, budget and delivery constraints.
openings.probe: Record order, cut and sewn dimensions, operator, design, direction and stage times. Measure offcut length and width through five washes. Check fit, wash survival and layout waste by area before releasing corrections; count trial and coordination labor.
openings.uncertainty: First units may mislead; cloth and operator effects unresolved. Small-cover timing does not establish batch feasibility; weight-estimated waste does not establish area compliance.

openings.claim: Actual table dimensions or corner geometry may explain customer failures despite reference-table fit.
openings.discriminator: Compare measured dimensions and corner profiles separately; failure on dimension-matched rounded tables supports an independent corner effect.
openings.fit: Measurement preserves constraints; any pocket revision requires validation.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner outlines from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders. Pair reference fit with observed first placement; compare similarly dimensioned tables with different corners. Validate resulting revisions for ordered design, tool-free removal and five-cycle survival.
openings.uncertainty: Customer accuracy, informative comparisons and timely participation unknown; missing matched comparisons remain inconclusive.

lineage.reason: With A1; retains shrinkage and area-waste checks.
With Z1; retains per-size release and confound tracking.
With A2; retains independent corner discriminator and revision checks.
With Z2; retains actual-order mismatch and reference/customer pairing.

post_distill.decision: Probe both; causes and 38/40 placement, all-design and 32-minute targets remain unproven. Honor ordered sizes/designs; use purchased stock with <=8% area waste, two machines, <=350 units and three weeks. Include all measurement labor; require five-cycle survival and tool-free removal.
